## 1. Project goal and data sources

PBS Utah wants to identify current non-major donors who are likely to reach
$1,200 or more in annual giving. The immediate outcome is conversion within 12
months; if the historical data supports it, the longer-term outcome will be
conversion within 3-5 years. This analysis uses constituent, payment, legacy
giving, soft-credit, campaign, Passport viewing, cultivation, and
officer-portfolio data.

The purpose of this EDA is to assess data quality, coverage, and useful
patterns before building a time-based prediction model. All records in this
release are synthetic, so no row represents a real constituent or gift.

```{r}
#| label: list-source-files

# This check makes the expected source files explicit before any analysis.
expected_files <- c(
  "constituents_w_memberships.csv",
  "unite_payments.csv",
  "team_approach_legacy_payments.csv",
  "soft_credits.csv",
  "campaign_codes.csv",
  "campaign_members.csv",
  "passport_viewing.csv",
  "cultivation.csv",
  "officer_portfolios.csv"
)

tibble(file = expected_files, exists = file.exists(file.path(data_dir, expected_files)))
```

## 2. Data inventory and grain/key documentation

These datasets have different grains, including one row per constituent,
payment, solicitation, or constituent-year-genre. They should not be joined at
the raw-row level because doing so can duplicate records. Transactional datasets will later be aggregated to a common donor-fiscal-year grain before modeling.

| File | Row represents / type | Unique key and links | Rows / unique constituents | Coverage | Data-quality findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `constituents_w_memberships.csv` | One constituent snapshot; attribute table | Constituent ID; referenced by most datasets | 196,167 / 196,167 | End-of-data snapshot; no dates | No missing or duplicate IDs; no duplicate rows; ages are 0–120. |
| `unite_payments.csv` | One payment; transaction table | payment_id; donor_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → campaign code | 1,722,698 / 71,643 IDs (71,642 matched constituents + SYN-ORPHAN) | FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-30 | Content-based valid-twin checks remove 36,044 invalid-link or nonpositive copies; 1,686,654 rows remain. Synthetic labels are audit-only. |
| `team_approach_legacy_payments.csv` | One legacy gift/payment; transaction table | No unique transaction ID. ta_account_id is a repeating household account; constituent_id_1–_7 → Constituent ID | 1,202,857 / 109,284 linked constituents | 1983-07-26 to 2020-06-28, pre-FY2021 | All amounts are positive. Cleaning removes 216,128 rows with no linked constituent before allocation, leaving 986,729 retained rows. |
| `soft_credits.csv` | One soft credit; transaction table | Credit ID; Soft Credit Constituent ID → Constituent ID | 4,145 / 3,028 IDs (3,027 matched + SYN-ORPHAN) | FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-29 | Exact duplicates are removed first; valid-twin checks then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive copies. Total removal: 192 rows; 3,953 remain. |
| `campaign_codes.csv` | One marketing/campaign code; reference table | Marketing Code; used by campaign members and payments | 29,249 / n.a. | No transaction date; includes initiative fields | No missing or duplicate keys or rows. All records are marked Active and Solicitation. |
| `campaign_members.csv` | One constituent solicitation/campaign-membership record; workflow/operational table | No unique key. constituent_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → Marketing Code | 5,233,404 / 181,680 | FY2021–FY2026; campaign markers 2020-07-01 to 2025-07-01; responses through 2026-06-30 | Links are complete and valid. 56,689 exact duplicate rows; constituent/code pairs repeat in 58,786 rows, sometimes valid under the documented solicitation rules. |
| `passport_viewing.csv` | One constituent × fiscal year × genre viewing record; behavioral attribute table | Composite constituent_id + fiscal_year + genre; constituent ID → Constituent ID | 444,741 / 70,515 | FY2021–FY2026 | Composite key is unique; all IDs link; no duplicate rows; viewing counts are positive and watch percentages are within 0–1. |
| `cultivation.csv` | One constituent-year portfolio assignment; workflow/operational table | Composite synthetic_id + fiscal_year; IDs → Constituent ID and portfolio_id → officer portfolios | 4,000 / 2,398 | FY2022–FY2025 | Composite key is unique; all links and binary flags are valid; no duplicate rows. |
| `officer_portfolios.csv` | One officer portfolio; workflow/reference table | portfolio_id; referenced by cultivation | 8 / n.a. | Rollout FYs: 2023–2026 | No missing or duplicate keys or rows. |

**Key implications:** Payments, soft credits, campaign memberships, and Passport viewing are one-to-many relative to constituents and cannot be raw-joined without duplicating records. Campaign-member repeats are retained because they can represent valid solicitations. Content-based valid-twin checks remove copied Unite-payment and soft-credit rows, while unlinked legacy rows are removed before allocation. Individual giving uses non-organization direct payments plus soft credits, so organization-payment dollars are not double counted. Current constituent attributes are end-of-data snapshots and will need time-aware handling later to prevent leakage.

## 3. Raw data quality checks

### Loading and structural checks

The following code loads the raw files and verifies their basic structure before any transformations or joins. This creates a compact baseline for checking that each expected file is readable and has the expected scale.

```{r}
#| label: loading-and-structural-checks

# Standardize names immediately after import so all later code can use
# consistent snake_case column names.
constituents <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "constituents_w_memberships.csv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
unite_payments <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "unite_payments.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
legacy_payments <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "team_approach_legacy_payments.csv"),
                            show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
soft_credits <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "soft_credits.csv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
campaign_codes <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "campaign_codes.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
campaign_members <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "campaign_members.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
passport_viewing <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "passport_viewing.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
cultivation <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "cultivation.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()
officer_portfolios <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "officer_portfolios.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()

raw_data <- list(
  "constituents_w_memberships.csv" = constituents,
  "unite_payments.csv" = unite_payments,
  "team_approach_legacy_payments.csv" = legacy_payments,
  "soft_credits.csv" = soft_credits,
  "campaign_codes.csv" = campaign_codes,
  "campaign_members.csv" = campaign_members,
  "passport_viewing.csv" = passport_viewing,
  "cultivation.csv" = cultivation,
  "officer_portfolios.csv" = officer_portfolios
)

structural_summary <- imap_dfr(raw_data, ~ tibble(
  file_name = .y,
  total_rows = nrow(.x),
  total_columns = ncol(.x),
  exact_duplicate_rows = nrow(.x) - nrow(distinct(.x)),
  total_missing_values = sum(is.na(.x))
))

knitr::kable(structural_summary, format = "pipe")
```

This structural check is designed to identify unexpected file sizes, schema
differences, exact duplicate records, and missing-data volume before detailed
quality checks begin. It does not make cleaning decisions or interpret any
findings.

### Missing-data checks

Missingness must be assessed by column because it can reflect unavailable
information, an unknown value, or a valid absence of activity.

```{r}
#| label: missing-data-checks

missing_data_summary <- imap_dfr(raw_data, function(data, file) {
  map_dfr(names(data), function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]

    tibble(
      file_name = file,
      column_name = column,
      missing_na = sum(is.na(values)),
      percent_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(values)),
      blank_strings = if (is.character(values)) {
        sum(!is.na(values) & trimws(values) == "")
      } else {
        0L
      }
    )
  })
}) |>
  filter(missing_na > 0 | blank_strings > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_missing))

knitr::kable(missing_data_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 1)
```

### Key and duplicate checks

Repeated activity is not always a duplicate: a donor can have many payments or
solicitations. Duplicates must therefore be evaluated using each dataset's
documented key.

```{r}
#| label: key-quality-checks

key_specs <- list(
  constituents = c("constituent_id"),
  unite_payments = c("payment_id"),
  campaign_codes = c("marketing_code"),
  passport_viewing = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year", "genre"),
  cultivation = c("synthetic_id", "fiscal_year"),
  officer_portfolios = c("portfolio_id")
)

key_quality_summary <- imap_dfr(key_specs, function(key_columns, dataset_name) {
  data <- get(dataset_name)
  missing_key <- reduce(map(key_columns, function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]
    is.na(values) | (is.character(values) & trimws(values) == "")
  }), `|`)

  valid_keys <- data |>
    filter(!missing_key) |>
    select(all_of(key_columns))

  duplicate_key_rows <- valid_keys |>
    group_by(across(all_of(key_columns))) |>
    summarise(rows_per_key = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(rows_per_key > 1) |>
    summarise(rows_in_duplicated_keys = sum(rows_per_key)) |>
    pull(rows_in_duplicated_keys)

  tibble(
    dataset = dataset_name,
    total_rows = nrow(data),
    rows_with_missing_key = sum(missing_key),
    distinct_keys = nrow(distinct(valid_keys)),
    rows_in_duplicated_keys = replace_na(duplicate_key_rows, 0L)
  )
})

knitr::kable(key_quality_summary, format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: exact-duplicate-row-checks

exact_duplicate_summary <- imap_dfr(raw_data, ~ tibble(
  file_name = .y,
  exact_duplicate_rows = nrow(.x) - nrow(distinct(.x))
))

knitr::kable(exact_duplicate_summary, format = "pipe")
```

### Relationship and link checks

These checks verify whether foreign keys can be linked to their documented
parent tables before later aggregation. An unmatched ID does not automatically
mean an error because the synthetic data includes documented `SYN-ORPHAN` and
legacy-data exceptions.

```{r}
#| label: relationship-and-link-checks

relationship_specs <- tribble(
  ~child_dataset, ~child_key, ~parent_dataset, ~parent_key,
  "unite_payments", "donor_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "soft_credits", "soft_credit_constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "unite_payments", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "passport_viewing", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "synthetic_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "portfolio_id", "officer_portfolios", "portfolio_id"
)

relationship_quality_summary <- pmap_dfr(
  relationship_specs,
  function(child_dataset, child_key, parent_dataset, parent_key) {
    child_data <- get(child_dataset)
    parent_data <- get(parent_dataset)

    child_ids <- child_data |>
      transmute(foreign_key = as.character(.data[[child_key]]))
    parent_ids <- parent_data |>
      transmute(parent_key_value = as.character(.data[[parent_key]])) |>
      distinct()
    unmatched_ids <- child_ids |>
      anti_join(parent_ids, by = c("foreign_key" = "parent_key_value"))

    tibble(
      child_dataset_foreign_key = paste0(child_dataset, "$", child_key),
      parent_dataset_key = paste0(parent_dataset, "$", parent_key),
      total_child_rows = nrow(child_data),
      unmatched_child_rows = nrow(unmatched_ids),
      distinct_unmatched_ids = n_distinct(unmatched_ids$foreign_key)
    )
  }
)

knitr::kable(relationship_quality_summary, format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: legacy-payment-link-checks

legacy_constituent_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)
legacy_link_matrix <- legacy_payments |>
  select(all_of(legacy_constituent_columns)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |>
  as.matrix()

legacy_has_link <- rowSums(
  !is.na(legacy_link_matrix) & trimws(legacy_link_matrix) != ""
) > 0
legacy_ids <- legacy_link_matrix[
  !is.na(legacy_link_matrix) & trimws(legacy_link_matrix) != ""
]
constituent_ids <- as.character(constituents$constituent_id)

legacy_link_summary <- tibble(
  total_legacy_rows = nrow(legacy_payments),
  rows_with_no_linked_constituent = sum(!legacy_has_link),
  percent_rows_with_no_linked_constituent = 100 * mean(!legacy_has_link),
  nonmissing_legacy_constituent_ids = length(legacy_ids),
  unmatched_legacy_constituent_ids = sum(!legacy_ids %in% constituent_ids)
)

knitr::kable(legacy_link_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 1)
```

### Value and date-range checks

These checks identify values outside plausible ranges and describe highly
skewed transaction amounts. An outlier is not automatically an error.

```{r}
#| label: transaction-amount-checks

amount_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "payment_amount",
  "legacy_payments", "payment_amount",
  "soft_credits", "credit_amount"
)

transaction_amount_summary <- pmap_dfr(amount_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- get(dataset)[[column]]
  percentiles <- quantile(
    values,
    probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )

  tibble(
    amount_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    zero_values = sum(values == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    negative_values = sum(values < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentile_25 = percentiles[1],
    median = percentiles[2],
    percentile_75 = percentiles[3],
    percentile_95 = percentiles[4],
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

knitr::kable(transaction_amount_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: range-and-validity-checks

summarise_range_validity <- function(values, field, lower_bound, upper_bound) {
  tibble(
    field = field,
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_below_lower_bound = sum(values < lower_bound, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_above_upper_bound = sum(values > upper_bound, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

range_validity_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_range_validity(constituents$age, "constituents$age", 0, 120),
  summarise_range_validity(passport_viewing$titles_viewed,
                           "passport_viewing$titles_viewed", 0, Inf),
  summarise_range_validity(passport_viewing$mean_percent_watched,
                           "passport_viewing$mean_percent_watched", 0, 1)
)

knitr::kable(range_validity_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: date-range-checks

date_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "credit_date",
  "legacy_payments", "gift_date",
  "soft_credits", "credit_date",
  "campaign_members", "campaign_start_date",
  "campaign_members", "responded_date"
)

date_range_summary <- pmap_dfr(date_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- as.Date(get(dataset)[[column]])
  nonmissing_dates <- values[!is.na(values)]

  tibble(
    date_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) min(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA),
    maximum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) max(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA)
  )
})

knitr::kable(date_range_summary, format = "pipe")
```

### Summary of data quality findings
The raw tables contain 79 exact soft-credit duplicates and 56,689 exact campaign-member repeats. Campaign-member repeats are retained because a constituent can legitimately receive more than one solicitation. Soft-credit duplicates are removed as the first step of the completed valid-twin cleaning process.
Missingness is concentrated in fields that are either unavailable in this synthetic release or structurally blank. Several University degree/employment fields, legacy descriptive and premium fields, and campaign_description are entirely missing. Campaign response_type and responded_date are missing for most records because most solicitations did not receive a response. Spouse and marital-status fields are also largely incomplete, while only two age values are missing. The constituent table is an end-of-data snapshot, so its fields will require time-aware handling later to avoid using information that would not have been available at a historical prediction date.
Most foreign-key relationships are complete. The raw unmatched payment and soft-credit IDs use the documented SYN-ORPHAN placeholder, which is reported only as an audit check. Completed content-based valid-twin cleaning removes 36,044 Unite-payment copies and 192 soft-credit copies; the former includes 1,225 invalid campaign-code copies, while the latter includes 79 exact duplicates. It also removes 216,128 unlinked legacy rows before allocation. Amounts contain no negative values; nonpositive copies with valid twins are included in the verified removals, while large gifts are retained as plausible outliers. All checked dates and Passport viewing ranges were valid.


## 4. Cleaning decisions

The raw imported tables remain unchanged. The following rules will be applied
only when creating analysis-ready copies.

| Issue | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Unite payment copies | Remove only invalid donor-link, campaign-code-link, or nonpositive-amount rows when an otherwise identical valid twin exists. | Content-based twin checks avoid relying on synthetic ID labels. |
| Soft-credit copies | Remove exact duplicates first, then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive-amount rows only when a valid twin exists. | Prevents duplicate credit while retaining unmatched records that lack a valid twin. |
| Unlinked legacy copies | Remove rows with no populated linked constituent ID before allocation. | They cannot be assigned to an individual donor. |
| Campaign-member rows | Retain all rows, including exact repeats. | Repeats can be valid solicitations. |
| Negative amounts | No action required. | None were found. |
| Fields that are 100% missing | Exclude from future feature creation. | They contain no information. |
| Structurally missing campaign response fields | Do not impute. | Missing `responded_date` and `response_type` generally indicate no recorded response. |
| Missing Passport records | Do not treat as zero viewing. | Preserve missingness and coverage as a separate concept. |
| Missing age and other partially missing constituent fields | Retain as missing for now. | Any model imputation must later be fit using training data only. |
| End-of-data constituent snapshot fields | Do not use directly as historical predictors unless a time-valid version can be created. | They could introduce data leakage. |
| Unite payments with an unmatched marketing code | Retain the payment for giving totals; treat campaign information as unknown unless the code can be mapped later. | The payment remains valid for giving analysis. |
| Large gifts | Retain. | They are plausible donor behavior, not demonstrated errors. |

The next subsection applies these rules to create analysis-ready copies while preserving the raw tables.

### Creating analysis-ready copies

The following code creates new analysis-ready objects while preserving all raw
objects for audit. These copies apply only the documented record-level rules;
they do not aggregate transactions, impute values, or create modeling features.

```{r}
#| label: create-analysis-ready-copies

content_twin_key <- function(data, columns) {
  do.call(
    paste,
    c(
      lapply(data[columns], function(value) replace_na(as.character(value), "<NA>")),
      sep = "\u001f"
    )
  )
}

valid_constituent_ids <- as.character(constituents$constituent_id)
valid_campaign_codes <- as.character(campaign_codes$marketing_code)

# A valid twin matches every substantive field except the record ID and the
# field that makes the candidate invalid. Synthetic labels are audit-only.
unite_payment_columns <- names(unite_payments)
unite_payment_candidates <- unite_payments |>
  mutate(
    valid_donor_link = donor_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_campaign_link = marketing_code %in% valid_campaign_codes,
    valid_amount = coalesce(payment_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

unite_donor_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "donor_id"))
)
unite_campaign_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "marketing_code"))
)
unite_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "payment_amount"))
)

unite_payments_flagged <- unite_payment_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_donor_copy = !valid_donor_link &
      unite_donor_twin_key %in% unite_donor_twin_key[valid_donor_link],
    invalid_campaign_copy = !valid_campaign_link &
      unite_campaign_twin_key %in% unite_campaign_twin_key[valid_campaign_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      unite_amount_twin_key %in% unite_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_donor_copy | invalid_campaign_copy |
      nonpositive_amount_copy
  )

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy) |>
  mutate(
    positive_amount = valid_amount,
    campaign_code_matched = valid_campaign_link
  )

soft_credit_exact_duplicate <- duplicated(soft_credits)
soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication <- soft_credits |>
  filter(!soft_credit_exact_duplicate)
soft_credit_columns <- names(soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication)
soft_credit_candidates <- soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication |>
  mutate(
    valid_recipient_link = soft_credit_constituent_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_amount = coalesce(credit_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

soft_recipient_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "soft_credit_constituent_id"))
)
soft_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "credit_amount"))
)

soft_credits_flagged <- soft_credit_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_recipient_copy = !valid_recipient_link &
      soft_recipient_twin_key %in% soft_recipient_twin_key[valid_recipient_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      soft_amount_twin_key %in% soft_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_recipient_copy | nonpositive_amount_copy,
    positive_amount = valid_amount
  )

soft_credits_analysis <- soft_credits_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy)

legacy_id_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)
legacy_payment_candidates <- legacy_payments |>
  mutate(
    has_linked_constituent = if_any(
      all_of(legacy_id_columns),
      ~ !is.na(.x) & trimws(as.character(.x)) != ""
    ),
    remove_unlinked_copy = !has_linked_constituent
  )
legacy_payments_analysis <- legacy_payment_candidates |>
  filter(!remove_unlinked_copy)

campaign_members_analysis <- campaign_members

organization_constituents <- constituents |>
  filter(
    primary_constituent_type == "Organization" |
      str_detect(
        coalesce(as.character(constituent_type), ""),
        regex("Organization", ignore_case = TRUE)
      )
  ) |>
  select(constituent_id, primary_constituent_type, constituent_type)

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  mutate(organization_payment = donor_id %in% organization_constituents$constituent_id)

constituents_analysis <- constituents
passport_viewing_analysis <- passport_viewing
cultivation_analysis <- cultivation
officer_portfolios_analysis <- officer_portfolios
campaign_codes_analysis <- campaign_codes
```

## 5. Descriptive patterns in giving and engagement

### Giving patterns over time

Fiscal-year trends describe the available giving history but do not yet combine
all giving sources into the final donor-level modeling dataset.

```{r}
#| label: giving-patterns-over-time

fiscal_year_from_date <- function(date) {
  year(date) + if_else(month(date) >= 7, 1L, 0L)
}

unite_payments_fy <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  filter(positive_amount) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(credit_date))) |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    total_payment_dollars = sum(payment_amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    number_of_payments = n(),
    distinct_linked_donors = n_distinct(donor_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

soft_credits_fy <- soft_credits_analysis |>
  filter(positive_amount) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(credit_date))) |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    total_credited_dollars = sum(credit_amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    number_of_soft_credit_records = n(),
    distinct_linked_constituents = n_distinct(soft_credit_constituent_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

knitr::kable(unite_payments_fy, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
knitr::kable(soft_credits_fy, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
```

### Campaign activity and response patterns

Campaign-membership records represent solicitations, not unique donors or
gifts. A constituent can appear more than once, so both solicitation volume and
distinct constituents should be reported.

```{r}
#| label: campaign-activity-and-response-summaries

campaign_code_features <- campaign_codes_analysis |>
  select(marketing_code, communication_method, campaign_type, activity_type)

campaign_activity <- campaign_members_analysis |>
  mutate(
    fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(campaign_start_date))
  ) |>
  left_join(
    campaign_code_features,
    by = "marketing_code",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )

campaign_fy_summary <- campaign_activity |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    solicitation_records = n(),
    distinct_solicited_constituents = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    responses = sum(responded == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    response_rate = mean(responded, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

campaign_method_summary <- campaign_activity |>
  group_by(communication_method) |>
  summarise(
    solicitation_records = n(),
    distinct_solicited_constituents = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    responses = sum(responded == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    response_rate = mean(responded, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(response_rate))

knitr::kable(
  mutate(campaign_fy_summary,
         response_rate = scales::percent(response_rate, accuracy = 0.1)),
  format = "pipe"
)
knitr::kable(
  mutate(campaign_method_summary,
         response_rate = scales::percent(response_rate, accuracy = 0.1)),
  format = "pipe"
)
```

### Passport viewing coverage and engagement

A missing Passport viewing record does not necessarily mean no engagement: it
may reflect no linked account, no consent, or no viewing activity. Therefore,
viewing coverage must be reported before interpreting behavior.

```{r}
#| label: passport-coverage-and-genre-summaries

passport_constituent_year <- passport_viewing_analysis |>
  group_by(fiscal_year, constituent_id) |>
  summarise(
    titles_viewed = sum(titles_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_percent_watched = median(mean_percent_watched, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

passport_coverage_fy <- passport_constituent_year |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    constituents_with_viewing = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    total_constituents = nrow(constituents_analysis),
    passport_coverage = constituents_with_viewing / total_constituents,
    total_viewing_records = sum(
      passport_viewing_analysis$fiscal_year == first(fiscal_year),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    total_titles_viewed = sum(titles_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_titles_per_viewing_constituent = median(titles_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_percent_watched_per_constituent_year = median(
      median_percent_watched,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

passport_genre_summary <- passport_viewing_analysis |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarise(
    total_titles_viewed = sum(titles_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    distinct_viewing_constituents = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    median_percent_watched = median(mean_percent_watched, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(total_titles_viewed, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  arrange(desc(total_titles_viewed))

knitr::kable(
  passport_coverage_fy |>
    mutate(
      across(c(constituents_with_viewing, total_constituents,
               total_viewing_records, total_titles_viewed,
               median_titles_per_viewing_constituent), scales::comma),
      passport_coverage = scales::percent(passport_coverage, accuracy = 0.1),
      median_percent_watched_per_constituent_year = scales::percent(
        median_percent_watched_per_constituent_year,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    ),
  format = "pipe"
)
knitr::kable(
  passport_genre_summary |>
    mutate(
      total_titles_viewed = scales::comma(total_titles_viewed),
      distinct_viewing_constituents = scales::comma(distinct_viewing_constituents),
      median_percent_watched = scales::percent(median_percent_watched,
                                                accuracy = 0.1)
    ),
  format = "pipe"
)
```

### Cultivation and portfolio context

Cultivation fields describe staff workflow and possible intervention, not
natural donor behavior. They will not be used as standard predictive features
because selection or contact may be influenced by staff judgment.

  left_join(
    officer_portfolios_analysis,
    by = "portfolio_id",

  )

  distinct(fiscal_year, portfolio_id, capacity) |>

            .groups = "drop")

  summarise(
    assigned_constituents = n_distinct(synthetic_id),

    portfolios_with_program_adopted = n_distinct(
      portfolio_id[program_adopted == TRUE]
    ),

  ) |>

portfolio_summary <- cultivation_portfolio |>

  summarise(

    selected_constituents = sum(selected == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),

  ) |>
  arrange(portfolio_id)

knitr::kable(
